```{r}
#| include: false
# Helper to process files by pattern

generate_mcmc_plot <- function(dir_path, coef, fixed_sp){
  process_files <- function(file_list, phe_type_label) {
    param_list <- map(file_list, function(file) {
      model_data <- readRDS(file)
      genus <- sub(paste0("(.*?)_", phe_type_label, "\\.rds"), "\\1", basename(file))
      if (fixed_sp) {
        param_data <- ggs(model_data$samples) |>
          filter(str_starts(Parameter, fixed("beta["))) |>
          mutate(beta_index = as.integer(str_extract(Parameter, "(?<=beta\\[)\\d+"))) |>
          filter(beta_index >= 5)|>
          rename(ParameterOriginal = Parameter) |>
          mutate(Parameter = genus) |>
          mutate(waic = model_data$WAIC$WAIC,
                 converge = model_data$converge,
                 milk = model_data$mean_logml)
      } else {
        param_data <- ggs(model_data$samples) |>
          filter(str_starts(Parameter, fixed(coef))) |>
          rename(ParameterOriginal = Parameter) |>
          mutate(Parameter = genus)|>
          mutate(waic = model_data$WAIC$WAIC,
                 converge = model_data$converge,
                 milk = model_data$mean_logml)
      }

      return(param_data)
    })
    combined_param_data <- bind_rows(param_list) |>
      filter(Parameter != "Alnus") |>
      mutate(phe_type = phe_type_label)
    return(combined_param_data)
}
  # Collect files
  SOS_files <- list.files(dir_path, pattern = "SOS\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)
  EOS_files <- list.files(dir_path, pattern = "EOS\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)

  # Process each type
  sos_data <- process_files(SOS_files, "SOS")
  eos_data <- process_files(EOS_files, "EOS")

  combined_param_data <- bind_rows(sos_data, eos_data)
  combined_param_data$phe_type <- factor(combined_param_data$phe_type, levels = c("SOS", "EOS"))

  # Summarize
  summary_data <- combined_param_data |>
    group_by(Parameter, phe_type) |>
    summarise(
      median_value = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
      lower_2_5 = quantile(value, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
      upper_97_5 = quantile(value, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
      waic = first(waic),
      converge = first(converge),
      milk = first(milk),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(Sig = ifelse(lower_2_5 * upper_97_5 > 0, "*", ""),
           SigAlpha = ifelse(Sig == "*", 1, 0.2),
           Color = ifelse(median_value >0, "#0D0887FF" , "#FCA636FF")) 

  param_levels <- rev(unique(summary_data$Parameter))

  # Plot
  
  p1 <- ggplot(summary_data, aes(x = factor(as.character(Parameter), levels = param_levels), y = median_value,
                                 colour = Color)) +
    geom_point(aes(alpha = SigAlpha), size=3) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower_2_5, ymax = upper_97_5, alpha = SigAlpha), width = 0.4) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
    geom_text(aes(label = round(median_value, 3)),
              vjust = -0.7, size = 4) +
    scale_alpha_identity() +
    scale_color_identity() +
    guides(alpha = "none") +
    facet_wrap(~ phe_type, scales = "free_x") +  # flip x/y means free_x
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Estimate") +
    theme(
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14)
    ) +
      coord_flip()

  if (coef %in% c("sp_effect", "z_hex")) {
    p2 <- ggplot(combined_param_data, aes(x = value, fill = ParameterOriginal)) +
      geom_density(linewidth = 0.1, alpha = 0.5) +
      scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-50, 50)) +
      facet_wrap(~ Parameter, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
      labs(
        x = paste0("Posterior distribution of ", coef),
        y = "Density"
      ) +
      facet_grid(Parameter ~ phe_type, scales = "free_y") +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
      theme(
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0),
        panel.spacing = unit(0.4, "lines"),
        legend.position = "none"
      )
  } else if (coef == "spatial_effect") {
    p2 <- ggplot(combined_param_data, aes(x = value)) +
      geom_density(fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.5) +
      scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-100, 100)) +
      facet_wrap(~ Parameter, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
      labs(
        x = paste0("Posterior distribution of ", coef),
        y = "Density"
      ) +
      facet_grid(Parameter ~ phe_type, scales = "free_y")+
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
      theme(
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0),
        panel.spacing = unit(0.4, "lines")
      )
  } else {
    p2 <- ggplot(combined_param_data, aes(x = value)) +
      geom_density(fill = "skyblue", alpha = 0.5) +
      facet_wrap(~ Parameter, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
      labs(
        x = paste0("Posterior distribution of ", coef),
        y = "Density"
      ) +
      facet_grid(Parameter ~ phe_type, scales = "free_y")+
      # geom_text(data = summary_data, aes(x = median_value-3, y = 0, label = round(median_value, 3)), vjust = -1, size = 3) +
      geom_text(data = summary_data, aes(x = median_value+3, y = 0, label = paste0("gelman.diag: ", round(converge, 4))), vjust = -1, color = "red", size = 3) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
      theme(
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0),
        panel.spacing = unit(0.4, "lines")
      )
  }
  p <- list(coef_summary_plot = p1, coef_density_plot = p2, summary_data = summary_data)
  return(p)
}

source("~/phenology-urban/script/spatial_stats_model/prepare_data_genus_species.R")
```

# Spatial random effect with covariance (INLA)

$$w(\mathbf{s}_i) \sim \mathcal{GP}(0, \Sigma)$$
In INLA, the SPDE approach is a way to represent a continuous Gaussian Random Field (GRF) as a sparse Gaussian Markov Random Field (GMRF). The mesh is used to discretize continuous space so that the SPDE can be represented as a finite-dimensional sparse matrix system.

# Treat the spatial random effect as a random effect without covariance (MCMC)

$$w(\mathbf{s}_i) = u_{g_i},\ u_{g_i} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2_w)$$
```{r fig-grid}
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "The hexagonal grid used for spatial modeling in New York City."
#| warning: false
#| eval: true

points_in_buffer <- read_csv(paste0("~/phenology-urban/data/proc/urban/",city,"/tree_WU_500_buffer_PS.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

points_sf <- st_as_sf(points_in_buffer, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326, remove = F) |>
  st_transform(crs = 9311)
hex_size <- 5000
bbox <- st_bbox(points_sf)
hex_grid_geom <- st_make_grid(bbox, cellsize = hex_size, square = FALSE)
hex_grid <- st_sf(geometry = hex_grid_geom) |>
  mutate(hex_id = row_number()) |>
  mutate(centroid = st_centroid(geometry)) |>
  mutate(
    hex_lon = st_coordinates(centroid)[, 1],
    hex_lat = st_coordinates(centroid)[, 2]
  )

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = boundary, fill = "grey90", color = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = hex_grid, fill = NA, color = "black", size = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(
    data = st_join(points_sf, hex_grid, join = st_within) |>
      filter(year == 2020) |>
      mutate(hex_id = factor(hex_id)),
    aes(color = hex_id), size = 0.01
  ) +
  guides(col = "none") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Comparison of models

To compare the performance of different models, I used the `WAIC` (Widely Applicable Information Criterion) and the log marginal likelihood (`mlik`) as metrics. The WAIC is a measure of model fit that accounts for both the goodness of fit and model complexity, while the log marginal likelihood provides a measure of how well the model explains the data.

I set the **"No spatial effect" model as the baseline for comparison**. The differences in `WAIC` and log marginal likelihood (`mlik`) between each model and the baseline are calculated. 

-   For `mlik_diff`, a positive difference indicates that the model performs better than the baseline, while a negative difference suggests worse performance.
-   For `WAIC_diff`, a positive difference indicates better performance for the alternative model, while a negative difference suggests worse performance.

```{r}
#| label: compare_genus
#| include: true
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Comparison of genera model performance using WAIC and log marginal likelihood (mlik)."
#| warning: false
#| eval: true

mcmc_random_sp <- mcmc_random_sp |>
  mutate(model = "Random spatial effect without covariance (MCMC)") |>
  dplyr::select(milk, waic, Parameter, phe_type, model)
inla_sp <- inla_sp |>
  mutate(model = "Spatial random effect with covariance (INLA)")

compare_models <- bind_rows(
  mcmc_random_sp,
  inla_sp|>
    filter(milk_type == "log marginal-likelihood (integration)") |>
    select(-milk_type))|>
  mutate(Parameter = gsub(" ", "_", Parameter),
         group = ifelse(grepl("_", Parameter), "species", "genus"))|>
  group_by(Parameter, phe_type) |>
  mutate(
    waic_diff = waic[match("Random spatial effect without covariance (MCMC)", model)] - waic,
    mlik_diff = milk - milk[match("Random spatial effect without covariance (MCMC)", model)] 
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = c("Random spatial effect without covariance (MCMC)",
                                          "Spatial random effect with covariance (INLA)")),
         phe_type = factor(phe_type, levels = c("SOS", "EOS"))) |>
  rename(mlik = milk) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c("waic", "mlik"),
    names_to = "matrices",
    values_to = "value"
  )

ggplot(compare_models |> filter(group == "genus" & Parameter != "Alnus"), aes(x = Parameter, y = value, fill = model)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  facet_grid(matrices~ phe_type, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  # coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 200)) +
  labs(x = "Parameter", y = "Model comparison \n(Log marginal likelihood or WAIC)",
       fill = "Model") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.spacing = unit(0.8, "lines")
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: compare_sp
#| include: true
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Comparison of species model performance using WAIC and log marginal likelihood (mlik)."
#| warning: false
#| eval: true
ggplot(compare_models |> filter(group == "species"), aes(x = Parameter, y = value, fill = model)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  facet_grid(matrices~ phe_type, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  # coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 200)) +
  labs(x = "Parameter", y = "Model comparison \n(Log marginal likelihood or WAIC)",
       fill = "Model") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.spacing = unit(0.8, "lines")
  )
```


# Discussion

The **spatial random effect with covariance (INLA)** model:

    -   Very fast.
    -   WAIC is slightly higher than that of the MCMC model for most cases.
    -   SPDE mesh approximation is not fine enough.
    -   Results are sensitive to priors and may get stuck in local optima.

The **spatial random effect without covariance (MCMC)** model: 

    -   Provides higher confidence in inference.
    -   Provide more interpretable estimates of spatial heterogeneity, not requiring the latent spatial field to be Gaussian.
    -   Less efficient (though still acceptable, ~2 hours for all models in NYC).
    -   The 5,000 m grid size may need further consideration.
